title: Carbonic Anhydrase Activity Assay
author: Jack C Koch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j4hcqt6
materials: Stock 50mM barbital buffer Mix 1 vial of barbital buffer (Sigma B5934-1VL) with 800 mL of deionized water. Once all powder is dissolved, add deionized water to 1L.

steps.title: Prepare Veronal Buffer A
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL of 50 mM barbital buffer with 250 mL deionized water, adjust the pH to 8.2 with 1 M HCl to obtain 25 mM Veronal Buffer (Buffer A).

steps.title: Prepare Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL of 50 mM barbital buffer with 250 mL deionized water, add 0.93 g EDTA and 1.23 g MgSO₄, stir until fully dissolved, then adjust the pH to 8.2 with 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Label Pipette Tips
steps.instruction: Take three new 1 mL pipette tips, mark one “A” for Buffer A, one “E” for Extraction Buffer, and one “C” for CO₂‑saturated seawater; use a fresh set of tips for each anemone native and denatured sample.

steps.title: Prepare CO₂‑Saturated Water
steps.instruction: In a 500 mL flask add 300 mL chilled deionized water, bubble CO₂ through an air stone for 15 min, twist a rubber stopper onto the flask and let CO₂ equilibrate for another 15 min; measure pH and keep the flask on ice. The target pH is < 4.00. If a CO₂ tank is unavailable, add 4–5 half‑dollar‑sized chunks of dry ice, loosely stopper the flask, allow pressure release, wait until the dry ice dissolves, then measure pH; repeat dry‑ice additions until pH < 4.00, finally tighten the stopper.

steps.title: Calibrate pH Probe
steps.instruction: Calibrate the pH probe daily according to the manufacturer’s specifications before any measurements.

steps.title: Set Up Assay Beaker
steps.instruction: Rinse a 6–12 mL sample vial/shell vial (Thomas Scientific 60975L‑3, 224744, 224745, 60965D‑1, or 60965D‑3) – referred to as the “beaker” – with 1 mL Buffer A, discard the wash, retain the stir bar, add 2 mL Veronal Buffer A using the “A” tip, place the beaker on ice, put a stir bar inside, and keep the beaker on ice during measurements.

steps.title: Run Native Sample Assay
steps.instruction: Place the beaker on a stir plate, insert the pH probe (ensure it is submerged and the stir bar does not hit the probe), start a “read/log” on the pH meter, quickly add 1 mL CO₂‑saturated seawater, watch the pH drop, wait at least 120 s before stopping the reading to confirm a rate of ~‑0.01 pH · s⁻¹, then rinse the beaker with DI water and discard the rinse (careful not to lose the stir bar). Repeat this whole sequence three times for the same native sample to obtain triplicate replicates.

steps.title: Process Anemone Tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh and remove between ½ and ⅛ of each A. elegantissima anemone (minimum ≈0.2 g frozen). From the unused portion, cut a diagonal slice from the oral cavity to the outer edge, place it in a 1.5 mL snap tube labeled “ALGAE + ID”, and freeze for later analysis. Finely mince the remaining tissue with a razor blade, transfer it to a glass‑Teflon tissue homogenizer containing 3 mL Extraction Buffer, keep the grinder on ice and grind for 1–1.5 min until no large chunks remain. Pour the homogenate into a 15 mL tube labeled with the anemone ID (native), keep on ice. Rinse the grinder with 4 mL Extraction Buffer, swish, grind a few more times, and add the rinse to the homogenate to obtain a total of 7 mL. Vortex briefly, then centrifuge at 4 °C, 4300 RCF for 10 min (balance the rotor). Transfer the supernatant to the “Native” tube; optionally freeze the pellet for future work. Using a P1000 pipettor, add 3 mL of the supernatant to the “Denatured” tube. Remove 200 µL–1 mL of the homogenate and place it in a 1.5 mL tube labeled “PROT + ID” for later Bradford protein assay, then freeze.

steps.title: Denature Sample
steps.instruction: Fill a 1000 mL beaker with ~900 mL deionized water, place on a hot plate and bring to a rolling boil. Loosen the cap of the “Denatured” tube slightly to allow pressure equilibration, insert the tube into a hole on a floating platform, and submerge it in the boiling water for exactly 5 min. Remove the tube and place it on ice for 5 min to cool.

steps.title: Run Denatured Sample Assay
steps.instruction: Rinse the beaker with 1 mL Buffer A, discard the wash, add 1 mL Veronal Buffer A (using the “A” tip), vortex/pipette‑mix the denatured homogenate briefly, add 1 mL denatured homogenate to the beaker, place the beaker on the stir plate, insert the pH probe (submerged, stir bar clear of probe), start a “read”, quickly add 1 mL CO₂‑saturated seawater, watch the pH drop, wait at least 120 s, stop the reading, then rinse the beaker with DI water (careful not to lose the stir bar). Repeat this entire sequence three times to obtain triplicate denatured replicates.

steps.title: Save Measurement Data
steps.instruction: Transfer all pH‑vs‑time data files from the pH meter to a flash drive or computer log for backup.

steps.title: Calculate CA Activity
steps.instruction: For each run, compute the slope (ΔpH/Δtime) using Slope = (y₂‑y₁)/(x₂‑x₁) where x is time in seconds and y is pH. Identify the most negative slope (largest absolute change) for that run. Average the three replicate slopes for native and for denatured samples separately, convert the average slope from per second to per minute, and record raw CA activity (ΔpH · min⁻¹). Measure protein concentration of the “PROT” sample with a Bradford assay, convert to mg mL⁻¹, and normalize CA activity by dividing raw CA / minute by the protein concentration (mg mL⁻¹) to obtain ΔpH · min⁻¹ · mg⁻¹ protein.
